purpose: Measure the timing of visible liquid-surface movement in the clip-released rig and its return to a settled level after the controller stops.
rig: A withdraws from the graduated cup. B returns liquid into the cup. A positive displacement in the selected trials follows the expected transfer direction. The camera measures a local projected surface height in pixels.

timing.time_zero: The host transmission timestamp precedes the firmware full-drive acknowledgement. The measured interval between them brackets software launch. The done timestamp is host receipt of the board stop report. Serial transport adds delay. The capture helper converts camera presentation timestamps onto the host monotonic clock. The physical sensor exposure and electrical edge have no independent common marker.
timing.time_resolution: Use frames.csv to index decoded frames rather than nominal MP4 playback time. The first visible displacement and later settling carry a frame of sampling uncertainty plus unmeasured sensor timestamp bias.
timing.firmware: Restored appliance image d6e49a5f6. Current source entry points are firmware/src_appliance/machine.cpp, claimPump, machinePumpRun, and endPumping.
timing.source_helper: tools/gun-positioner-observation/helper/main.swift. A null helper_drop_count means the capture ended without the optional device summary. Frame counts match decoding and separate per-frame timestamp records.

surface_method.view: Upright 1180 by 830 crop of the 1920 by 1080 stream. Pixel rows increase downward. Four eleven-pixel green-channel strips center on x=117, 129, 141 and 153. A Gaussian vertical blur of 3 px precedes interpolation at brightness values 23, 27 and 31. The starting coarse camera reading selects the nearby descending edge. Subsequent frames follow the nearest crossing with a positive drop across the edge. A fixed printed feature at [229,184,112,63] is matched in every frame and its vertical movement is subtracted.
surface_method.quality: Tracks require valid crossings in 88% of frames and 85% of each reference window, with the signed endpoint excursion exceeding 8 px. The median of 1.5 to 0.15 s before command and 2.0 to 3.65 s after completion defines each settled change. Track ranges are sensitivity to viewing position and edge choice. Their shared optical errors preclude treating them as independent replicates.
surface_method.response: First of four consecutive frame timestamps above the greater of a 2.5 px excursion and the pre-run 95th percentile absolute fluctuation; a three-frame median suppresses isolated excursions. The central slope is Theil–Sen over 20% to 80% of the timed gate.
surface_method.after_stop: Positive excess indicates that the optical boundary has gone beyond its settled position in the transfer direction. The early window is 0.05 to 0.21 s after completion. Later window medians are at 0.4–0.6, 0.9–1.1 and 1.9–2.1 s. The settling time is the first frame after the last excursion of the five-frame median beyond the specified band, inspected through 3.4 s after completion. Zero indicates the signal stayed inside the band from the first post-completion frame. The band is the greater of 3 px and twice the median track’s settled 95th-percentile fluctuation.

long_hold.method: With no further pump commands, correlate each vertical green edge profile against the median at 5–10 s, allowing a fitted brightness gain and offset. The three clear strips have a change above 20 digital counts across 10 px. Reference their shifts to the fixed upper-left printed feature. Endpoint shifts are comparable to local image fluctuation and registration sensitivity.

interpretation: A moving surface can overshoot and return after stop, particularly on filling. The response time describes the chosen local optical threshold. Flow onset at either tube tip, individual motor revolutions, and continued delivery after stop require independent measurements.
